children: Indian benchmark indices extended their winning streak for a second consecutive session on November 17, with the Nifty reclaiming the 25,500 mark intraday for the first time since February 2026, led by gains in auto, banking and realty stocks.

Despite weak global cues, the markets opened on a flat note but gained momentum in the early hours, with the Nifty touching an intraday high of 25,501.35 in the first half of the session. However, selling pressure emerged in the afternoon, trimming some of the gains. Nevertheless, the benchmarks managed to hold on to positive territory, supported by sustained foreign fund inflows, easing crude oil prices, and further depreciation in the rupee.
At close, the Sensex was up 427.40 points or 0.52 percent at 82,532.19, and the Nifty was up 96.30 points or 0.38 percent at 25,387.40.
Biggest Nifty gainers were M&M, Axis Bank, Eicher Motors, Asian Paints, Interglobe Aviation, while losers included HCL Technologies, Power Grid Corp, Coal India, HDFC Life and Infosys.
Among sectors, IT index shed 0.9% and FMCG index fell 0.3%, while Realty and PSU Bank indices rose nearly 2% each, media, metal, oil & gas, auto, private bank, infra up 0.5-0.9%.
The broader indices ended mixed, with Nifty midcap index rising 0.3 percent, while smallcap index fell 0.22 percent.

Among individual stocks, Sigma Advanced Systems shares gained 5% after the company announced a strategic joint venture with Spain-based Escribano Mechanical & Engineering (EM&E Group). Senco Gold gained 5% after reporting record festive sales and Greaves Cotton advanced 6% after surpassing its entire FY26 registration count.
SML Mahindra shares rose 5% after the company's board approved raising up to Rs 1,450 crore, while, Kaynes Technology shares declined 4% after Jefferies cut its target price to Rs 3,625 per share.

More than 140 stocks touched 52-week high, including stocks of Angel One, PNB, Motilal Oswal, Billionbrains Garage, Honasa Consumer, Allied Blenders, Emcure Pharmaceuticals, PVR INOX, DLF, Union Bank, Eternal, Ramkrishna Forgings, among others. Click to View More

The Indian rupee extended its gains for a second consecutive session, appreciating 46 paise to close at 93.47 against the US dollar on November 17, compared with the previous session's close of 93.93.
Shrikant Chouhan, Head Equity Research, Kotak Neo

The benchmark indices continued their positive momentum. The Nifty ended 96 points higher, while the Sensex was up by 428 points. Among sectors, the PSU Bank and Realty indices rallied nearly 2 percent, whereas intraday profit booking was seen in select IT stocks; as a result, the IT index shed nearly 1 percent.

Technically, on the daily and intraday charts, the market is holding a higher-high and higher-low formation, which supports the continuation of the uptrend in the near future. For trend-following traders, 25300/82300 would now act as a key support zone. As long as the market is trading above the same, the bullish formation is likely to continue. On the higher side, 25500/82800 would act as an immediate resistance zone for the bulls. Above the same, the rally could continue till 25600-25650/83000-83500. On the flip side, below 25300/82300, the uptrend would become vulnerable. Below the same, traders may prefer to exit their long trading positions.
Vatsal Bhuva, Technical Analyst at LKP Securities

Nifty closed with a bullish candlestick formation on the daily chart, indicating sustained buying interest. The index is currently consolidating within a defined range of 25,200–25,500. The broader undertone remains bullish, and a buy-on-dips strategy should be preferred by index traders.

Some consolidation is likely before the next leg of upward momentum unfolds. On the downside, 25,200 remains an immediate support, while 25,500 is the immediate resistance. Nifty is expected to gradually move higher and test the next resistance zone of 25,800.
